name: What does performance mean?
purpose: Before measuring performance, a performance theory must stipulate five things.

parts.label: (b) Standards
points: Expectations associated with each performance level

parts.label: (c) Situational constraints
points: How (if at all) to weight factors outside the employee's control

parts.label: (d) Number of levels
points: How many performance levels or gradients

parts.label: (e) Absolute vs relative
points: Compare with a standard or with colleagues (ranking)?

apply: Use (a)–(e) as the design checklist for any PM system in a case
Ask first: what is value-adding work here? (Beach House: innovation, not output)
pitfalls: Jumping to a rating form before defining what performance means for this job
example: Role play: manager and employee disagree on the appraisal – the key issue is a different understanding of performance.

name: Evaluation systems shape behaviour
purpose: What behaviours does each evaluation system encourage?

parts.label: Team evaluation on a case study

apply: Predict the behaviour the case's system rewards – and compare it with the behaviour the firm needs
pitfalls: Evaluating a system only by its accuracy – its behavioural effects matter more

name: Why firms drop traditional appraisals
purpose: What is pushing organizations to drop annual appraisals and embrace alternatives?

parts.label: Return of people development
points: Tight labour markets: firms must grow talent
Frequent coaching conversations instead of a yearly rating

parts.label: Need for agility
points: Short-term, flexible goals and frequent check-ins

parts.label: Centrality of teamwork
points: Feedback from several people, team goals

apply: Check which of the three pressures applies to the case firm
Recommend continuous feedback, development focus or team goals accordingly
pitfalls: Claiming appraisals disappear completely – firms still need decisions on pay and promotion

name: Forced distribution: disadvantages
origin: Session 5 · ranking on a normal curve
purpose: Why does ranking employees on a forced curve backfire?

parts.label: Demotivation of the majority in the middle
Infighting and reduced collaboration
points: Why work with the stars if they push you into the bottom 10 %?

parts.label: Horse-trading
points: Lobbying and politicking before reviews, trading favours

apply: If the case uses rankings, list the disadvantages that already show and propose absolute standards plus development conversations

name: Purposes of a PM system
purpose: What is the new system FOR? Each purpose pulls the design in a different direction.

parts.label: Accountability
points: Evaluate and decide: pay, promotion, exit

parts.label: Development
points: Needs trust, frequent and forward-looking talks

parts.label: Communication
points: Clarify goals and expectations, align with strategy

apply: State the main purpose for the case firm first
Then design to it – and explain the tension (rating for pay hurts honest developmental talk)
pitfalls: Trying to serve all purposes with one annual meeting

name: Designing a PM system (Beach House)
origin: Beach House case · key feedback points
purpose: Which design choices must a performance management proposal decide and justify?

parts.label: Control vs autonomy
points: Structure and targets vs freedom to experiment

parts.label: Quantitative vs qualitative indicators
points: Countable output vs judgement of quality, ideas, behaviours

parts.label: One system vs segmented
points: Can the “A Team” be managed like the “Tweakers”, given the nature of their work?

apply: 1. Name the key problem (Beach House: lack of innovation)
2. Define value-adding activities for each group
4. Set each slider and justify it
5. Analyse potential externalities (what will people stop doing?)
pitfalls: Measuring innovators with output targets – that kills the innovation you want
Forgetting the limits of PM: not everything valuable can be measured (“Humanize”)
